quizName:
Hardest Questions in Arkansas
									  					
									  														  					Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Pull over and take a break.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and take a break.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop at a rest area or service station to take a break, nap, or stretch. Caffeine pills and energy drinks are not safe replacements for rest.

questions.question: When must drivers follow posted speed limits?
questions.explanation: Always obey posted speed limits. Check your speedometer often to make sure you are driving at a legal speed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for people with disabilities

questions.correctAnswerText: Reserved parking for people with disabilities
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces for people with disabilities. Only vehicles with disabled license plates, Disabled Veteran plates, or disabled parking permits can use these spaces.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for traffic on your right

questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this location. You must obey this sign.

questions.question: What should you do if you encounter an aggressive driver?

options.text: Let them pass and stay out of their way

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass and stay out of their way
questions.explanation: The safest choice is to let aggressive drivers pass and get out of their way. Do not compete with other drivers. Always focus on safe driving.

questions.question: In Arkansas, is wearing a front seat belt required by law?

options.text: Yes, it is required by law

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is required by law
questions.explanation: In Arkansas, you must wear a seat belt if you are the driver or a front seat passenger. Wear your seat belt every time you drive, not just on long trips.

questions.question: When you see a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, what should you do?

options.text: Honk to let them know you are there

questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog means the person is blind or has low vision. Always give pedestrians with these tools the absolute right-of-way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn at this location. You cannot turn around to go in the opposite direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Left turn allowed only after stopping
All traffic must turn right at the next intersection

questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through a symbol means that action is not allowed. This sign means left turns are prohibited.

questions.question: What type of road condition does this sign warn about?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns you that another road crosses ahead.

questions.question: Who can park in handicap parking spaces?

options.text: Anyone, but only if all other spaces are taken
Only drivers with a disabled license plate or parking permit
Anyone who is not feeling well

questions.correctAnswerText: Only drivers with a disabled license plate or parking permit
questions.explanation: Only people with disabilities can use handicap parking spaces. You must have the correct license plate or hanging permit to park there.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign alerts you to a steep hill coming up. Slow down to avoid losing control or damaging your brakes.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that U-turns are not allowed at this location.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings warn drivers of hazards ahead. Round signs only warn about railroad crossings.

questions.question: Like alcohol and drugs, drowsiness can:
questions.explanation: Lack of sleep causes poor driving. Drowsiness slows your reaction time, reduces awareness, and harms your judgment—just like drugs and alcohol.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, you should:

options.text: Speed up to cross before the train arrives.
Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
Find a way around any lowered gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs alert you to possible trains ahead. Always obey these signs and never drive around barriers or ignore flashing signals.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Wet roads are slippery and dangerous. This sign warns you to slow down because wet pavement makes it harder to stop your car.

questions.question: If you get tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: When tired, the best choice is to stop and rest or switch drivers. Fatigue dulls your thinking and slows your reactions, making driving unsafe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has curves.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn in the direction of the arrow. In this case, right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.explanation: This sign is posted on one-way streets and places where you cannot enter. You may see it if you try to enter an expressway ramp in the wrong direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go the opposite direction at this location.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle is coming toward you with flashing red or blue lights?

options.text: Pull to the right side of the road and stop completely.
Keep driving, but stay out of its way.
Drive faster to reach your destination before it catches up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: The law requires you to move out of the way for police cars, fire trucks, and ambulances using sirens and flashing lights. Pull to the right edge of the road. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before pulling over.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with no safety gate, you should:

options.text: Assume no trains usually cross there.
Look both ways to check for a train before crossing.
Quickly cross if you think you can beat an oncoming train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look both ways to check for a train before crossing.
questions.explanation: At a crossing with no safety gate, look both ways for trains before crossing. If a train is coming, stop at a safe distance and wait. Never try to outrun a train.
